【目标与棋盘】\n可选 9 路、13 路、19 路。路数就是纵横交叉线的数量。9:
[Board and goal]
Choose a 9×9, 13×13 or 19×19 board. You play black and move first. Your friend plays white. Enclose more area than your opponent.

[Stones, liberties and captures]
Take turns placing one stone on an empty intersection. Stones stay where they are placed. Stones of the same colour connected horizontally or vertically form a group. Empty adjacent intersections are liberties; diagonal neighbours do not count. A group with no liberties is captured and removed.

[Legal moves]
You cannot play on an occupied intersection. Captures are resolved before checking your own liberties. A move that leaves your group without liberties is not allowed. Positional superko prevents any move that recreates a previous board position.

[Passing and scoring]
Use Pass when you have no further move to make. After two consecutive passes, click groups to mark or unmark dead stones. You confirm dead groups yourself; the opponent does not decide this automatically. Scoring counts living stones and empty intersections surrounded by only one colour. Neutral points do not count. White receives 7.5 points of komi on all board sizes.

[Controls]
Click an intersection to place a stone. The paper beside the board has Pass, How to play, Resign and New game. To change board size, return to the game selection.
【目标与先后手】\n使用 15 × 15 棋盘，你执黑先行，AI 执白。双方轮流:
[Board and turns]
Play on a 15×15 grid. You take black and move first; your friend takes white. Take turns placing one stone on an empty intersection.

[Winning]
Connect five or more stones of your colour in an uninterrupted horizontal, vertical or diagonal line. Empty intersections or opposing stones break a line. A full board with no winner is a draw.

[Rules used here]
This is freestyle Gomoku. There are no double-three or double-four restrictions; a line longer than five also wins. There is no swap opening, capturing or moving stones after placement.

[A small tip]
Watch your opponent as well as your own line. If they have four connected stones, block them. Lines open at both ends offer more possibilities.

[Controls]
Click an intersection to place a stone, then wait for the response. The paper beside the board lets you read the rules, restart, resign or choose another game.
【目标与先后手】\n棋盘为 8 × 8。你执白先行，AI 执黑。目标是将死对方的:
[Board and goal]
The board is 8×8. You play white and move first. Win by checkmating the opposing king: it is under attack and no legal move can remove the threat. The king is never actually captured.

[Moving pieces]
King: one square in any direction, never into check.
Queen: any distance horizontally, vertically or diagonally.
Rook: any distance horizontally or vertically.
Bishop: any distance diagonally.
Knight: two squares in one direction and one across; it can jump over pieces.
Pawn: one square forward, or two from its starting square if both squares are clear. It captures one square diagonally forward and never moves backwards. White pawns move up the board, black pawns down. Only knights may jump over pieces.

[Check and legal destinations]
If your king is in check, move it, block the attack or capture the attacking piece. A move that leaves your king in check is illegal. Select one of your pieces to see its legal destinations marked with dots.

[Castling]
If the king and the relevant rook have not moved, the intervening squares are empty, and the king is not in check and does not pass through or finish on an attacked square, move the king two squares towards the rook. The rook moves beside it automatically.

[En passant and promotion]
Immediately after an opposing pawn advances two squares and lands beside your pawn, you may capture it diagonally on the square it crossed. This option lasts only for your next move. A pawn reaching the final rank must promote to queen, rook, bishop or knight. Choose the promotion on the paper before moving.

[Draws]
A player with no legal move whose king is not in check is stalemated. Common insufficient-material positions are draws. This game automatically draws after a position repeats three times, or after 50 moves by each side without a pawn move or capture; it simplifies the usual claim procedure.

[Controls]
Select a white piece, then its destination. Selecting another white piece changes your selection. The paper lets you review the rules, resign or start again.
